turn1.explanation: The unit fires on clause- and list-boundary punctuation (commas, periods, semicolons) in running prose. It fires most strongly when the document has a ship/boat/maritime theme (even a loose one such as the word 'anchor'), and more weakly on the same punctuation in documents with no such theme.
turn1.evidence: The top examples are SeaArk boats, power ships, a cruise-ship casino, Swedish listed ships, flying boats and V.Ships; their commas and periods reach 3.5–4.2, while the words around them stay near 0. Non-maritime prose gets moderate values: news broadcasting (~2.5), a medical CT report (~1.5) and a legal oil-rig case (~1.2); the Anchor-electronics privacy page and the 'anchor text' SEO page reach ~3.
turn1.missing_data: Punctuation-dense non-maritime texts compared directly against maritime texts, to confirm the topic effect rather than general prose style. Also whether ship words alone, without following punctuation, ever activate the unit.
